history.summary: The tokens that let a theme have a type voice, and the re-pointing pass that makes them real. registry/tokens/typography.css now separates the PALETTE (--font-sans/-serif/-mono) from the ROLES components read (--font-heading/-body/-ui) and adds the four heading-voice knobs (--heading-weight/-tracking/-transform/-leading). Every consumer moved: 72 family references across 64 stylesheets, classified by role rather than renamed in bulk — controls and floating chrome to --font-ui (44), content surfaces to --font-body (17), headings to --font-heading, and the eleven var(--doc-font, …) chains keeping the document face first with the body role as their floor. Ten heading surfaces that only inherited a family now name the role (card/dialog/drawer/sheet/alert-dialog/callout/empty-state titles, the stat value, every pattern headline). --heading-tracking is 0em, not the plan's 0: calc(-0.01em + 0) is invalid CSS and would have silently dropped the heading primitive's optical tightening; with a unit, a theme's tracking ADDS to a heading's own. No visual change was measured, not argued — every canonical fragment rendered in Chromium before and after, all six type properties compared element by element: 4,160 elements x 6 readings, four differences, all one deliberate fix (a callout and a page-break inside a data-variant="report" document used to render sans inside a serif page, because the variant set font-family while they read var(--doc-font, …); the variant now re-points --doc-font for its subtree). gen:theme-manifests produced 84 pure insertions across 12 manifests with zero deletions — tokens_inherited only. The docs generator needed real work: it derived a token's preview property from its name prefix, which the heading-* family breaks (each drives a different property), so HEADING_VOICE_PROPERTY names them and the typography page grew a Font roles section and a Heading voice section. tests/tokens/role-tokens.test.ts (28 cases) is the permanent gate.

The baseline was intermittently red and the engine was innocent: tests that assert on work a MutationObserver delivers were spending a FIXED number of await tick()s waiting for it. The main partition shares one process and one happy-dom realm, so a late file inherits ~170 files' worth of pending effects and timers, and the delivery lands a turn further out than the test allowed. Measured on a clean tree at 1f36b0f: tests/recipes/tree-view-reactive.test.ts failed 3 full-suite runs in 4 (aria-posinset "1" where the reorder makes it "2"), tests/core/lifecycle.test.ts's late-append l-cloak case took the fourth — every one of them green alone, green in its own directory, green with tests/core/ alone; bisection found no single polluting file, only the accumulated queue, which is exactly what a tick count cannot be calibrated against. happy-dom delivers observer callbacks on a real microtask (MutationObserverListener.report → window.queueMicrotask), so the waits were not wrong in principle, only in assuming one turn is always enough. tests/helpers/settle.ts adds settle(condition, what, turns): poll one turn at a time, return the moment the condition holds (the already-satisfied path costs no turns), throw naming the awaited behavior when the 50-turn budget runs out, and treat a throwing probe as not-settled so a test can address a node the pending work has yet to create. The two flakes now wait for the refresh instead of for a turn; lifecycle.test.ts's 'two turns' comment, which predicted this exact failure, is gone with it. tests/meta/settle.test.ts (11 cases) is the permanent gate, in the two halves spawn-timeouts.test.ts uses: behavioural proof that settle() waits, returns early and fails legibly, plus a source gate over tests/ and packages/ banning any NEW consecutive await tick() pair. Six older boot/mount helpers (faqir-mask, inbox, engine-page — two each) are allow-listed rather than converted blind, each needs a condition chosen by someone reading what it boots, and the gate fails in BOTH directions so a converted site must be delisted instead of the list becoming documentation of a habit. The gate was proven non-vacuous by planting a pair and watching it go red. Verification: 5 full-suite runs, 4 green (207 files); run 2's single failure was a 60s spawn budget expiring with empty stdout while bun run typecheck's seven tsc passes competed for the machine, and run 3 hit the runner's 20-minute partition cap having printed no test output at all — a bun-level wedge before any file reported, the class commit c2fc2d7 already names. Neither is this suite's assertion timing, and the flake this task targets did not recur once. Found while verifying 1.1A-02's baseline, which is why 1.1A-02 did not run.

The two families a theme needs to state a silhouette and a ring. registry/tokens/effects.css publishes the shape ladder (--border-width-sm/-md/-lg), the two ROLES components name (--border-width, --border-width-strong), --corner-shape, and the five focus tokens (--focus-ring-width/-offset/-style/-color, --focus-shadow) — 11 tokens, 13 with the --card-border-width / --input-border-width silhouette aliases 1.1A-05 will aim at; the theme surface moved 241 → 254 and gen:theme-manifests produced 156 PURE insertions across 12 manifests, zero deletions. base/reset.css's :focus-visible spells out nothing any more, and the gate fails on a bare length or colour appearing in it. Every literal edge in the primitives is gone: 40 border widths in 22 files and 13 outlines in 13 files, classified rather than renamed in bulk — the default edge to --border-width (including the four forced-colors rules), emphasis to --border-width-strong where the design leans on a thicker rule (kbd's keycap bottom, nav's active indicator, separator[data-weight=thick], collapsible's chevron, the spinner ring and button[data-state=loading]'s), --border-width-lg for the spinner's 3px, and the alias on card/input/textarea/select. --focus-shadow is consumed in reset AND in all 13 primitive rings, because a control's own :focus-visible (0,2,0) outranks reset's (0,1,0) — declared only in reset the glow axis would have reached bare elements and no button. The inset rings read calc(-1 * var(--input-border-width)) so the ring keeps covering the edge when a theme thickens it. No visual change was MEASURED: every registry fragment rendered in Chrome 149 before and after with every focus rule forced on, four border sides plus outline width/style/offset and box-shadow compared element by element — 4,093 elements x 8 readings, ZERO differences; corner-shape is supported by that engine and computes to its initial `round` on all six surfaces. Two shim findings shaped the CSS: happy-dom drops any border shorthand resolving to an oklch() colour (so the in-suite proof swaps colours for hex), and it mis-splits var(--a, var(--b)) in a shorthand's width slot, which is why the aliases are named at one level. tests/tokens/shape-focus.test.ts (38 cases) is the permanent gate, proven non-vacuous by planting a literal; tests/base/prose.test.ts's value index needed the shape and focus families excluded — left in, --border-width-md: 2px claimed prose's text-underline-offset.
